STAGE 1 APPLICATION  
 
1.1 
ACCESSING APPLICATION PORTAL 
 
1. Login to https://admission.sutd.edu.sg/. 
 
2. Enter your User ID and password as per your MyPortal login. 
 
3. Click on Sign In. 
 
 
 
4. Click on Start a New Application. 
 
5. Select Outbound under Application Type. 
 
6. Select Global Exchange Programme under Application Programme. Note: SUSEP students to 
select Global Exchange Programme as well, you will be linked to SUSEP application page. 
 
7. Click on Next. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

[PAGE 3]
Page 3 of 12 
Office of International Relations 
Updated as of September 2023 
1.2 
COMPLETING APPLICATION 
 
1. Read the application instructions for each section carefully. 
 
2. You will be required to submit the following information. 
 
• 
Personal Particulars (pre-filled) 
• 
Contact Information (pre-filled) 
• 
Offered / Intended Pillar  
• 
Choice of Host University  
• 
Participation in Overseas Programmes 
• 
Special Assistance Required 
• 
Vaccination Information 
• 
Exchange T-shirt Size 
• 
Essay 
• 
Upload of Portfolio/Resume 
• 
Application Declaration 
 
3. Once each section has been completed, click on Next. 
 
4. You may click on Save and return to complete the application. 
 
5. Check your application summary and click on Submit. This is the final submission and no 
changes will be allowed after submission. 
 
6. You will receive a system automated email to confirm that your application has been received. 
The application status will be shown as Submitted. 
 
7. Click on Outbound under Application Type to view your application summary.  
 
 
 
8. Click on the page numbers at the top to view your application details.

STAGE 2 APPLICATION – UPDATE STUDY 
 
PLAN & CREDIT TRANSFER FORM

ACCESSING STUDY PLAN 
 
1. Login to https://admission.sutd.edu.sg/. 
 
2. Enter your User ID and password as per your MyPortal login. 
 
3. Click on Sign In. 
 
4. Click on Update Study Plan. 
 
 
 
 
2.2 
UPDATING STUDY PLAN (TERM 4, 5, 7 & 8) 
 
1. Click on the search button to update the courses you plan to take / taken in Term 4, Term 5, 
Term 7 and Term 8. 
 
2. Click on the plus or minus sign to add or delete course. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

[PAGE 5]
Page 5 of 12 
Office of International Relations 
Updated as of September 2023 
2.3 
UPDATING STUDY PLAN (TERM 6) 
 
1. Your host university choices will appear under “Courses you plan to take in Term 6” 
section. 
 
2. Click on Edit to update the Study Plan for each host university. 
 
 
 
3. For courses in the Reference Course List: 
 
• 
Click on the search button to select the Partner University Course 
• 
Click on the search button to select the corresponding SUTD Course 
 
 
 
4. For new courses NOT in the Reference Course List: 
 
• Key in the Partner University Course ID, Course Title and Course Credits 
• Click on the search button to select the corresponding SUTD Course 
• Select the Partner University Course Level (Bachelor / Master) 
• Complete the Credit Transfer Form 
 
5. Click on the plus or minus sign to add or delete course. 
 
 
 
6. Key in minimum 8 Pillar-related Courses and 2 HASS-related Courses. 
 
7. Click on Save after completing the Study Plan and Credit Transfer Forms.  
 
 

[PAGE 6]
Page 6 of 12 
Office of International Relations 
Updated as of September 2023 
2.4 
UPDATING STUDY PLAN (GEXP - UCEAP) 
 
 
1. If UCEAP is one of your host university choice, submit 4 Study Plans (one for each campus), 
as required by UCEAP. 
 
2. For every Partner University Course that you add, indicate which UCEAP Campus it is from.  
 
3. For each UCEAP campus, key in minimum 8 Pillar-related Courses and 2 HASS-related 
Courses. In total, your UCEAP Study Plan should have 32 Pillar-related Courses and 8 HASS-
related Courses. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

[PAGE 7]
Page 7 of 12 
Office of International Relations 
Updated as of September 2023 
2.5 
UPDATING CREDIT TRANSFER FORM    
        
1. Key in the following information for each Credit Transfer Form for Pillar/HASS’s 
review if the course is suitable for credit transfer. 
 
• 
Partner University Course Department 
• 
Partner University Course Credits 
• 
Course Description 
• 
Website Links 
• 
Mode of Assessment and Breakdown 
• 
Workload and Breakdown 
• 
Upload Course Syllabus 
 
2. Click on the plus or minus sign to add or delete items. 
 
3. Click on Save after you have completed the Credit Transfer Form. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

[PAGE 8]
Page 8 of 12 
Office of International Relations 
Updated as of September 2023 
2.6 
SUBMITTING STUDY PLAN 
 
1. You may click on Save Draft, and return to complete the Study Plans. 
 
2. After completing all the Study Plans for each host university, give it a last check on 
the main page. 
 
3. Click on Submit at the bottom of the page. This is the final submission and 
no changes will be allowed after submission. 
 
4. Submission will be routed to Pillars for review. Host university will not be considered for 
offer if Study Plan is incomplete or there are insufficient credit transfer information for 
Pillar review. 
 
 
 
5. You will receive a system automated email to confirm that your study plan has been received. 
The application status will be shown as Processing. 
 
6. Click on Outbound under Application Type to view your application summary.  
 
 
 
7. Click on the page numbers at the top to view your application details, study plans and credit 
transfer forms.

3 
SUBJECT DECLARATION  
 
3.1 
ABOUT SUBJECT DECLARATION 
 
1. Students who miss the subject declaration period will not be eligible for credit transfer. 
 
2. Subject declaration is to be completed after course enrolment at host university.  
 
3. Before subject declaration period, ensure study plan is updated and subjects taken at host 
university are approved in the Online Application Portal.  
 
4. During subject declaration period, no updates can be made to the study plan (cannot edit 
subjects or add new subjects). 
 
5. Subjects must be approved by Pillars/HASS in the Online Application Portal, otherwise please 
seek email approval from Pillars/HASS immediately (appeals are subjected to review by 
Pillars/HASS).  
 
6. Declare up to 48 SUTD subject credits for credit transfer. No overloading is allowed during 
exchange.  
 
7. No changes will be allowed after submission.  
 
 
3.2 
ACCESSING SUBJECT DECLARATION 
 
1. Login to https://admission.sutd.edu.sg/. 
 
2. Enter your User ID and password as per your SUTD MyPortal login. 
 
3. Click on Sign In.  
 
4. Click on Subject Declaration. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

[PAGE 10]
Page 10 of 12 
Office of International Relations 
Updated as of September 2023 
3.3 
SUBMITTING SUBJECT DECLARATION 
 
1. Select the Subject Declaration for each subject. 
 
• 
Not Taken at Partner University 
• 
Taken at Partner University for Audit / Interest (Not for Credit Transfer) 
• 
Taken at Partner University for Credit Transfer (this option will only appear for approved 
courses) 
 
2. Click on Save after you have completed the Subject Declaration. This is the final submission 
and no changes will be allowed after submission. 
 
 
3. You will receive a system automated email to confirm that your Subject Declaration has been 
received.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

[PAGE 11]
Page 11 of 12 
Office of International Relations 
Updated as of September 2023 
4 
CREDIT TRANSFER  
 
4.1 
ELIGIBILITY FOR CREDIT TRANSFER 
 
  
1. Students who missed the credit transfer period will not be eligible for credit transfer. 
 
2. Submit credit transfer request, along with your official transcript and grades (once available) to 
your Pillar for review and approval.  
 
3. Subjects must be approved by Pillars/HASS in the Online Admission Portal and declared during 
the subject declaration period.  
 
4. Transfer up to 48 SUTD subject credits. No overloading is allowed during exchange. 
 
5. Obtain passing grade (according to host university’s transcript and grading system). 
 
6. Meet minimum number of credits for credit transfer. 
 
7. Taken for Letter Grade (not Pass/Fail/Credit/Non-Credit option). 
 
8. Complete all pre-programme and post programme deliverables. 
 
9. No misconduct during exchange. 
 
10. No changes will be allowed after submission.  
 
11. Credits earned will be counted towards SUTD degree and reflected in SUTD transcript. Grades 
received will not be counted towards CGPA. 
 
4.2 
ACCESSING CREDIT TRANSFER 
 
1. Login to https://admission.sutd.edu.sg/. 
 
2. Enter your User ID and password as per your MyPortal login. 
 
3. Click on Sign In.  
 
4. Click on Credit Transfer. 
 
 
 
 
 
 

[PAGE 12]
Page 12 of 12 
Office of International Relations 
Updated as of September 2023 
4.3 
SUBMITTING CREDIT TRANSFER 
 
1. Key in the Grade / Marks for each subject taken at the host university. 
 
2. Click on Add Attachment to upload the host university official transcript. 
 
3. Read the declaration and tick the box. 
 
4. Click on Save after you have completed the Credit Transfer Request. This is the final 
submission and no changes will be allowed after submission. 
 
5. You will receive a system automated email to confirm that your Credit Transfer Request has 
been received.

IS THERE ANY MINIMUM CGPA REQUIREMENT FOR 
APPLICATION? 
No, there is no minimum CGPA requirement for application. 
However, students are required to meet the host university 
minimum CGPA (based on student’s CGPA at the time of 
application), nationality and other requirements to be 
considered for exchange placement for that particular host 
university. 
IS THERE AN APPLICATION INTERVIEW?
No, there is no application interview. Applications will be 
reviewed based on the eligibility criteria. Exchange placements 
are allocated based on ranked university choices and available 
quota, subject to suitability of study plan and host university’s 
requirement (such as minimum CGPA, nationality, and other 
criteria). There will be a balloting process if the quota is 
exceeded.
WHAT IS THE BALLOTING PROCESS?
When the number of eligible students exceeds the available 
quota for a host university, a balloting process will be 
conducted based on students’ ranked university choices. 
Students who ranked the university as their 1st choice will be 
prioritised first, followed by those who ranked it as their 2nd, 
3rd, and 4th choices. If the number of students within the same 
choice ranking exceeds the remaining quota, a random ballot 
will be conducted to determine the placement.

TICKETS AND ACCOMMODATION?
Book your flight tickets and make accommodation 
arrangements only after receiving the official acceptance 
letter from your host university. Follow the host 
university instructions for visa application (if any), on-
campus accommodation application and any other 
required preparations. If you are contacting the host 
university for enquiries, please do so respectfully as a 
responsible SUTD Ambassador, be mindful of office hours 
and allow reasonable response time. 
FAQ - PRE-DEPARTURE
IS IT COMPULSORY FOR ME TO PURCHASE SUTD 
STUDENT TRAVEL INSURANCE?
Yes, it is compulsory to ensure you are adequately 
covered. No waiver is allowed. The insurance coverage 
can be found on MyPortal (Student Matters and Policies > 
Student Matters > Student Insurance Scheme). If host 
university and/or visa application requires you to 
purchase separate travel/health insurance, you will need 
to purchase both. Waiver is subjected to review and 
approval by host university.
HOW CAN I PAY FOR SUTD STUDENT TRAVEL 
INSURANCE?
It can be paid online via internet banking. Look out for 
email instructions and make payment timely before 
departure.
GEXP Information Deck 
Copyright Global Student Mobility

[PAGE 79]
IS HOST UNIVERSITY’S ORIENTATION 
COMPULSORY? IS IT POSSIBLE TO GIVE IT A MISS?
You are required to complete the full exchange 
programme at your host university, including any 
compulsory orientation and examinations. Even if 
orientation is not mandatory, do attend as it is a good 
platform to make new friends, and learn important and 
useful information which are usually shared during 
orientation. 
CAN I OPT FOR OFF-CAMPUS ACCOMMODATION 
ALTHOUGH HOST UNIVERSITY OFFERS ON-CAMPUS 
ACCOMMODATION?
Yes, you can opt for off-campus accommodation. 
However, staying on campus is generally more 
affordable. If you are staying off-campus, do check the 
rental regulations and any additional charges. Ensure the 
location is safe and do not sign any contract until you are 
agreeable to all terms. It is not advisable for ladies to stay 
alone outside of campus for safety reasons
FAQ - PRE-DEPARTURE
MAY I PARTICIPATE IN EXTRACURRICULAR 
ACTIVITIES IN HOST UNIVERSITY?
Yes, you are encouraged to participate in extracurricular 
activities to expand your network and meet friends from 
different backgrounds. Talking to people and taking up 
new hobbies may also ease your anxiety in a new 
environment. Do be mindful of high-risks sports and 
activities and ensure you have adequate insurance 
coverage.
DO I NEED TO BE FLUENT IN MY HOST COUNTRY’S 
LANGUAGE? 
Though most host universities do not require students to 
be fluent in their local language upon arrival, it is good to 
learn some basic phrases before departure. Some host 
universities may offer basic language classes for 
students. An ability to understand the language will help 
you better adapt to the new environment.

[PAGE 2]
Academic matters
Courses for  
exchange students
At least 2/3 of the courses should be selected from one school. The re-
maining 1/3 can be taken from other Schools of Technology in Aalto Univer-
sity, as long as the prerequisites are met.
Exchange students are not allowed to take courses from the School of Arts, 
Design and Architecture or the School of Business, except for cross-school 
courses, university wide studies and interdisciplinary studies. For more 
information on studies, please see website. 
There are some changes in the course selection every year, the study 
programmes are updated during the summer. Students must be prepared to 
make changes in their study plans upon arrival.
Regardless of study level, exchange students can choose both Bachelor 
and Master level courses, provided that the prerequisites are met. The ma-
jority of courses offered in English are on the Master level.
Academic calendar
Autumn Term 2025
August - December, periods I and II
Teaching and exams 31 Aug – 13 Dec 2026
Orientation is held on the week before the teaching starts (24 - 30 Aug). 
Exact dates will be confirmed later.
Spring term 2026
January - July, periods III, IV and V
Teaching and exams 11 Jan – 13 June 2027
Orientation is held before the teaching starts. Exact dates will be confirmed 
later.
Grading and credits
The grading scale is 1-5 (1 is the lowest passing grade and 5 the highest) or 
pass/fail.
The scope and workload of courses is given in ECTS credits (=Europe-
an Credit Transfer System). One credit corresponds to 27 hours of work, 
including lectures and other forms of instruction, exercises, seminars and 
independent work at home and in the library. The scope of a course can be 
1-15 ECTS credits depending on its content. 
 
A full study load is 30 ECTS per term, which corresponds to about 800 
hours of studying. There are no set limits on how many courses students 
can take. However, Aalto University expects exchange students to study full 
time and pass courses with good grades. 
Transcript of 
records
Students can order a digitally signed transcript of records themselves. 
Signed and stamped paper version can be sent to the student on request.

[PAGE 3]
Applying
Nomination
The home university should nominate students to Aalto University with the 
following information: student’s name, exchange semester, e-mail address 
and intended study field in Aalto University. There is no set nomination 
deadline, but nominations should preferably be sent at least two weeks 
before the application deadline.
Application dead-
lines
April 30: Deadline for applications for the next autumn term and academic 
year
 
October 15: Deadline for applications only for the next spring term
 
Please verify the dates online.
How to apply
Nominated students receive application instructions and a link to the online 
application by email. Attachments are uploaded to the online application, no 
hard copies are required.
 
More detailed application information can be found on website (read also 
the schools specific application information under Incoming exchange stu-
dents for the schools of technology). 
Requirements
Academic requirements: Aalto University strongly recommends at least 
two to three years of Bachelor’s studies before arrival. 
Language requirements: Exchange students need either an official lan-
guage test certificate or a certificate from an English language teacher/
professor stating that the student has sufficient language skills to study 
in English in their subject area (minimum B2 in CEFR level). Only students, 
whose mother tongue is English or who study in English-medium pro-
gramme in a university in Australia, Canada, Hong Kong, Ireland, Singapore, 
the UK, or in USA, are exempted from providing a language certificate.
Application results
The application results will be ready within six weeks after the application 
deadline.

[PAGE 4]
Practical matters
Accommodation
Aalto University does not own any student housing nor have housing ser-
vices to offer. Main housing providers are HOAS (Foundation for Student 
Housing in the Helsinki Region) and AYY (Aalto University Student Union). 
Students must apply for housing themselves according to the instructions 
given by Aalto University. The housing situation in Helsinki metropolitan 
area is difficult, especially in the autumn. Aalto University cannot guarantee 
student accommodation for all exchange students. For more information on 
housing for exchange students, please see website.
Visa / residence  
permit
Citizens of non-EU/EEA countries must apply for visa or residence permit. 
Non-EU/EEA students are advised to start the residence permit applica-
tion process immediately after receiving the letter of admission. For more 
information on applying residence permit, please see Finnish Immigration 
Service (MIGRI) website.
Citizens of EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzer-
land do not need a residence permit for Finland but must register right of 
residence in Finland if non-stop stay exceeds 3 months. For more infor-
mation on registering an EU citizen’s right of residence, please see Finnish 
Immigration Service (MIGRI) website.
Insurance and 
health care
Students must personally cover costs if they become ill in Finland, therefore 
all exchange students must have insurance that is valid for the whole dura-
tion of the stay in Finland.
Students who apply for Finnish residence permit must take out private 
insurance that covers medical and drug expenses. For more information 
on eligible insurance for residence permit application, please see Finnish 
Immigration Service (MIGRI) website.
In addition to private insurance, EU-students should take European Health 
Insurance Card (EHIC) with them to Finland. By presenting the European 
Health Insurance Card, one can prove right to necessary medical treatment 
in another EU or EEA country and in Switzerland. The card must be valid for 
the whole duration of stay in Finland. 
Please note that exchange students do not have access to Finnish Student 
Health Services (FSHS).
The emergency number in Finland is 112. 
Living expenses
According to current estimate, students need 800 euros per month for 
living expenses. The total living expenses depend greatly on the type of 
accommodation. For the breakdown of estimated monthly expenses, please 
see website. 
Student Union 
Membership
AYY (Aalto University Student Union ) membership is optional but highly 
recommended for all exchange students. AYY membership is mandatory 
for students who live in AYY apartments. For more information on benefits, 
please see AYY website.

COURSE RESTRICTIONS
	› Undergraduate exchange students can only enrol in
a maximum of two Computer Science courses per
term. This includes courses cross-listed with Computer
Science.
	› View the full list of restricted courses.
	› Space is limited in our Architecture programs at
all levels. We will be reviewing nominations on a
first come first serve basis when nominations open.
The Undergrad Architecture Rome program will be
available in 2026-2027. Visit our website to learn more
about the Undergrad Architecture Rome program.
NOMINATIONS
	› Split quota between our fall, winter and spring terms
when possible.
	› Like many cities in Canada, Waterloo Region is experiencing
a housing shortage. On campus housing is extremely limited
and not guaranteed. Partners are encouraged to nominate
early so students can apply.

cannot guarantee students a spot. On campus accommodation
for both the fall and winter terms is extremely limited.
SPRING TERM
	› Waterloo offers full academic programming during our Spring
term (May to mid-August). Many courses are offered in spring
and all services, including Orientation, on-campus housing,
and student clubs are available.

[PAGE 4]

TERM DATES
Two terms of study are equivalent 
to a full academic year, although we 
operate on a trimester system with a 
full fall, winter, and spring term. Each 
term is four months and counts as 0.5 
FTE towards the exchange balance. 
Exchange students can study for one 
term or two terms.

NOMINATION PROCESS
Complete online for each student under the nominator login portal. You will receive an email when nominations open. Once 
approved, we will email the nominator and the student with detailed application instructions. 
ELIGIBILITY 
 UNDERGRADUATE 
Students must:
	› Be enrolled at one of the University of Waterloo’s exchange
partner institutions
	› Be nominated by their home institution as an exchange
applicant
	› Meet the University of Waterloo’s undergraduate English
language proficiency (or equivalent)
	› Have a 70% cumulative average or equivalent at their home
institution
 ARCHITECTURE APPLICANTS MUST ALSO HAVE: 
	› Completed at least two years of study (equivalent to four/
five terms is ideal) prior to the commencement of exchange
	› A 75% cumulative average or equivalent at their home
institution.
 GRADUATE 
	› Completed an Honours Bachelors’ degree or equivalent
and be actively enrolled in a graduate-level program at
one of the University of Waterloo’s exchange partner
institutions
	› 75% (or equivalent) overall standing in the past two years
of study
	› Be nominated by their home institution as an exchange
applicant
	› Meet the University of Waterloo’s graduate English
language proficiency (or equivalent)

[PAGE 5]
Come to Waterloo    |       5
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS  
Our application process is entirely online. We do not 
require hard copies of any documents. We aim to provide 
students with offer letters eight weeks after the application 
deadline. 
COURSE SELECTION PROCESS 
We cannot guarantee enrolment in any specific course, 
and it is important to be flexible during this process.  
Waterloo’s course registration process for undergraduate 
and graduate students occurs after admission.   
COURSE CREDIT SYSTEM 
 UNDERGRADUATE 
The full-time course load is five courses per term 
(equivalent to 2.5 units) with a minimum of three courses 
per term (equivalent to 1.5 units). Most courses are 
assessed as a unit of 0.5 and are approximately 39 teaching 
hours per term. 
 GRADUATE 
The full-time course load is one graduate course per 
term. Details of specific credit weights and teaching hours 
per course are available on the graduate schedule of 
classes. Most courses are assessed as a credit of 0.5 and are 
approximately 39 teaching hours per term.
LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS
All incoming exchange students must have sufficient 
English language skills to be successful in their exchange. 
Students may be required to submit proof of English 
language proficiency prior to admission to the exchange 
program.
 UNDERGRADUATE 
Students should provide a digital copy of their English 
language proficiency scores or equivalent documentation 
supporting their language proficiency
See complete English language requirements for more 
information.
 GRADUATE 
Students should provide English language proficiency 
certification (official test score or English language 
equivalency letter from the student’s home school)
See complete English language requirements for more 
information.
Come to Waterloo    |       5

[PAGE 6]
Come to Waterloo    |       6
IMMIGRATION DOCUMENTS 
Review our Come to Waterloo - Immigration tab for more 
information 
TRANSCRIPT
An official Waterloo transcript will be available for students 
to share in electronic format with their home institution 
approximately two months following the end of their study 
term. Students will receive instructions once their transcript 
is ready to share.  
We do not send transcripts directly to the home school 
coordinator. 
FEES 
Students will be assessed for incidental fees, every term. Fees 
include mandatory health insurance and a student services 
fee that provides unlimited access to the regional transit 
system. All fees are approximate in Canadian dollars and are 
subject to change. Student Financial Services will post fees 
to students’ accounts approximately one month prior to the 
beginning of term, and fees must be paid before arriving at 
Waterloo. 
HEALTH INSURANCE
Students are enrolled in two health insurance plans. The 
University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) covers basic health 
care services, such as medical doctor appointments, hospital 
visits, and most diagnostic tests. The Studentcare extended 
Health and Dental Plan covers extra costs like prescription 
drugs, paramedical practitioners, vision, and dental care. 
Students can opt-out of extended health and dental 
insurance if they meet the criteria and can prove that they 
have equivalent coverage. Applications for UHIP exemption 
are only considered if students meet the criteria outlined on 
the UHIP website. 

[PAGE 7]
Come to Waterloo    |       7
ORIENTATION
It is strongly encouraged that students attend Exchange 
Orientation to experience a balanced introduction to 
the academic, social, and community aspects of life 
at Waterloo. Program details and dates will be sent to 
students closer to the start of the term.
ACCESSIBILITY
Waterloo is committed to ensuring all students can 
access and meaningfully participate in their education 
by removing barriers and building capacity for 
personal success. Students with permanent, temporary, 
or suspected disabilities are encouraged to contact 
AccessAbility Services to register for supports and 
services.
STUDENT SUPPORT 
International Peer Community (IPC) connects with 
fellow international students and upper-year student 
leaders. Together students engage in fun events to 
explore campus and the Kitchener-Waterloo area.
CLUBS, SPORTS AND RECREATION
Students can get involved through the Waterloo 
Undergraduate Student Association (WUSA) or the 
Graduate Student Association (GSA). Whether students 
are interested in food, politics, dance, business, gaming, 
or the environment, joining a club is the perfect way to 
find something students love and meet others who share 
that same passion.
Stay active and enrich wellness experience while at 
Waterloo by checking out our Athletics and Recreation 
facilities. Follow @WlooRec and @WlooWarriors for tips 
and events.
INTERNATIONAL AND CANADIAN 
STUDENT NETWORK (ICSN)
Community of fellow Canadian, international and 
exchange students. Together, students will build 
connections, participate in events, and get a taste of 
life in Waterloo. Follow @WUSAICSN on Instagram for 
upcoming events.
